OUTSIDER_TEAMS.TITLE: Microsoft Teams
OUTSIDER_TEAMS.DESCRIPTION: Handle Microsoft Teams conversations in Chatwoot. Each Teams bot connected here becomes an inbox: messages arrive as conversations and replies go back to Teams.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS.EMPTY: No Teams bot connected. Follow the steps above and click Connect a Teams bot.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS.CREATED: Bot connected. Paste the messaging endpoint in Azure and upload the app package to Teams.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS.DELETE_CONFIRM: Disconnect this Teams bot? The inbox and conversations stay in Chatwoot, but Teams messages stop arriving.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS.TEST_OK: Credentials are correct: Microsoft granted the bot access.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS.TEST_FAILED: Microsoft rejected the credentials. Check the app ID, secret and tenant ID. {message}
OUTSIDER_TEAMS.ENDPOINT_HELP: Paste it in Azure Bot > Configuration > Messaging endpoint. The address must be public (HTTPS).

FIELDS.NAME: Inbox name
FIELDS.KEEP_PASSWORD: Leave blank to keep the current secret
FIELDS.HELP: All three values are in Azure, on the bot you created (Configuration and Microsoft Entra ID). The secret is encrypted in Chatwoot and never shown again. Legacy multi-tenant bot: use botframework.com as tenant.

GUIDE.TITLE: How to connect Teams
GUIDE.AZURE: In the Azure portal, create an Azure Bot resource (app type: single tenant) and note the app ID and tenant ID (Configuration).
GUIDE.SECRET: In Configuration > Manage password, create a client secret and copy its value.
GUIDE.ENDPOINT: Here in Chatwoot, click Connect a Teams bot, fill in the three values and save. Copy the messaging endpoint and paste it in Azure Bot (Configuration > Messaging endpoint).
GUIDE.CHANNEL: In Azure Bot, under Channels, enable the Microsoft Teams channel.
GUIDE.PACKAGE: Click Download app package and upload the .zip in Teams (Apps > Manage your apps > Upload an app) or in the Teams admin center to release it to the company.
GUIDE.AGENTS: In the new inbox (Settings > Inboxes), add the agents who will reply. Use Test credentials to check.

OUTSIDER_TEAMS.BOT_SUBTITLE: the existing bot link, for people who talk to the company through Teams

OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.TITLE: Microsoft Teams
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.DESCRIPTION: Bring your chats and your teams' channels from Teams into Chatwoot.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.NOT_PUBLIC: Chatwoot is not on a public https address. Teams only sends new-message notices and the Office viewer only opens files when Chatwoot runs on its public address (FRONTEND_URL).
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.PRIVACY: each person sees only their own Teams. Administrators see only who connected and whether it works, never the conversations. Files stay in OneDrive and SharePoint; Chatwoot only shows them.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.MY_INTRO: Sign in with your work e-mail. You go to the Microsoft page and come right back.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.MY_DISCONNECTED: Your Teams is disconnected. Sign in again to get your chats and channels back.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.NEEDS_APP: IT has not registered the Teams app yet. Ask an administrator.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.DISCONNECT_CONFIRM: Disconnect your Teams? Conversations stop arriving here (nothing changes in Teams).
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.RECONNECT_HELP: Microsoft asked for a new sign-in (password changed or access reviewed by IT). Click Sign in again.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.ALL_CHANNELS_HELP: New channels come in by themselves. Untick the ones you do not want.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.WORKING: Bringing your channels and older messages from Microsoft. It can take a few minutes; this page updates by itself.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.NOTICES_NO_REASON: Microsoft did not answer. Save again to retry.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.WHAT_HELP: Only you see it. You can change it anytime.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.NO_TEAMS: You are not in any Teams team.
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.APP_INTRO: Done once by IT in Microsoft Entra ID. After that each person just clicks "Sign in with Microsoft".
OUTSIDER_TEAMS_GRAPH.SECRET_KEEP: leave blank to keep the current one
